title: Responsible AI
task_statement: Apply responsible AI duties to the system, with per-group evaluation and documented evidence. (Inference: repo lesson and general practice, not in the official mirror)

components.name: Content moderation with Claude
components.first_principle: Claude classifies user content against a written policy and labeled examples, so the policy text is the control.
steps: Collect examples of content to flag and content to allow.
Include edge cases in the examples, because edge cases test the policy.
Write the moderation categories from the examples.
Send each item with the policy and the categories to Claude.
Constrain the response to a schema, so the verdict is a parseable value.
Route uncertain or refused items to a person. (Inference)
pros: Handles semantic meaning and many languages without a separate model for each language.
Policy changes need prompt changes, not relabeled training data.
Gives a written reason that a reviewer can read.
cons: Built-in safety behavior can flag content that your own policy allows.
A refusal can leave the verdict empty, so the flow needs a fallback path.
Results depend on the policy text and the examples. (Inference)
use_when: User-generated text needs fast moderation decisions.
One process must cover several languages.
do_not_use_when: The rule is a fixed pattern, such as a blocked word list. A rule is cheaper. (Inference)
A person must make every decision for legal reasons. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Write the policy with examples that include edge cases.
constraints.combination: Test the examples again before each policy change. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Keep the policy text under version control with a review date. (Inference)
Use a smaller model such as Claude Haiku 5.5 for moderation when cost matters.
constraints.combination: Use a larger model for appeals. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Track flagged and refused items as a metric.
constraints.combination: Review repeat offenders before you throttle or ban an account.

native_services.text: Not in source. The moderation guide names no cloud platform for this workflow.

components.exam_tie: D5.5. Expect a scenario about user content, a policy that changes often, and several languages. The credited answer uses a written policy with examples and a structured verdict. (Inference)
components.trap: A custom classifier looks cheaper, but each policy change then needs new labels and code. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Put the moderation policy and examples in the prompt, and constrain the verdict with a schema.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario says the policy changes often, choose a prompt-defined policy over a retrained model.

components.name: Safety classifiers and refusal handling
components.first_principle: A refusal is a normal response with a stop reason, so the application reads the stop reason and handles the refusal in code.
steps: Read stop_reason on every response, also on streamed responses.
Treat a refusal stop reason as a normal response, not as an error.
Read stop_details.category to learn which policy area declined the request.
Set fallbacks to default, in beta, to retry a declined request on a fallback model.
Tell the user that the request was declined, and do not resend it unchanged. (Inference)
Log each refusal with its category and request ID, so repeat cases can be reviewed.
pros: Makes a declined request visible in application code.
Lets the application choose a fallback path.
Shows the policy category in logs and reviews.
cons: Server-side fallback is in beta, and Claude Haiku 5.5 does not support it.
A fallback model can change answer quality. (Inference)
Classifiers can decline a legitimate request. (Inference)
use_when: The product sends user text that may trip a classifier.
The product needs a retry path without an error page.
A team needs counts of declines by category.
do_not_use_when: The application ignores stop reasons and treats every output as final.
The retry must run on a model with a different data location. Check the platform terms first. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Log stop_details.category with the request ID.
constraints.combination: Alert when one category rises sharply. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use the server-side fallback to avoid a second client round trip.
constraints.combination: Use the SDK middleware for client-side fallback on platforms without server-side fallback.

constraints.choice: Throttle or ban a user only after repeated refusals of one kind.
constraints.combination: Keep a review step before any ban. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Read the stop reason in every streaming handler.

components.exam_tie: D5.5. Expect a scenario where a refused request breaks the flow. The credited answer reads the stop reason and handles the refusal in code. (Inference)
components.trap: A refusal treated as an HTTP error and retried unchanged. A refusal returns a normal response with a stop reason.
components.decision_rule: Read stop_reason on every response, and handle refusal as a normal outcome.
components.exam_tip: If a response has stop_reason refusal, do not parse it as an error.

components.name: Model documentation, transparency, and per-group evaluation
components.first_principle: Published model documentation gives context, and the team adds its own per-group evidence for its own users.
steps: Read the system card for the model that the product uses.
Read the Usage Policy before you build the product.
Check the Trust Center for security and trust material.
Evaluate the outputs by group, and do not use an aggregate alone. (Inference)
Set a floor for each group and hold the release until each group meets its floor. (Inference)
Name an owner for each decision class and record the evidence. (Inference)
pros: Gives published test context for each model.
Points to the Usage Policy that governs use.
Separates vendor evidence from your own evidence.
cons: System cards do not test your user population. (Inference)
An aggregate score can hide a weak group. (Inference)
Evaluation by group needs group labels, which many products lack. (Inference)
use_when: A product team must document the model that it uses.
A review asks for model evidence.
The team plans a model change.
do_not_use_when: The question is about your own product outputs. Use your own evaluation.
A sandbox test that never reaches users.

constraints.choice: Keep the system card link and the model ID in the release record.
constraints.combination: Require a new review when the model ID changes.

constraints.choice: Have a reviewer read the Usage Policy before launch.
Check the model deprecation page on a schedule.
constraints.combination: Plan a tested move before the retirement date.

constraints.choice: Use one evaluation set per user group that matters for the product. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Set a floor for each group. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D5.5. Expect a scenario that asks for evidence of responsible use. The credited answer cites the system card and the Usage Policy, then adds the team's own per-group evaluation. (Inference)

components.exam_tip: If the answer relies only on vendor documentation, add the team's own evaluation.

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{User content or model output?} -->|User content| B{Policy changes often?}
  A -->|Model output| C[Read stop reason on each response]
  B -->|Yes| D[Prompt policy with examples and schema verdict]
  B -->|No| E[Stable policy file with the same design]
  D --> F{Results differ by group?}
  E --> F
  C --> F
  F -->|Yes| G[Per group floor and upstream fix before release]
  F -->|No| H[Document evidence and name an owner]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  P[Written policy] --> E[Labeled examples]
  E --> V[Schema verdict]
  S[stop_reason refusal] --> D[Normal result path]
  D --> F[stop_details category]
  M[System card] --> O[Own evaluation]
  O --> G[Per group floor]

patterns.rule: Read stop_reason on every response. Handle refusal as a normal outcome.
traps: Treat refusal as a server error and resend the same request

patterns.rule: Check each group against its own floor before release. (Inference)
traps: Generated reasons that the trace does not support
